title: Smarter Men Possess More Masculine Body Shapes but Report Fewer Casual Sex Partners al-sex-partners/
author: Eric W. Dolan
summary: A new study reveals an intriguing relationship between cognitive ability and sexual behavior in young men. Researchers found that men with higher fluid intelligence—measured through visual pattern recognition tasks—tend to display markers of physical fitness such as greater grip strength and more V-shaped torsos, while paradoxically reporting fewer casual sexual partners. This finding contradicts simplistic evolutionary assumptions that physical attractiveness uniformly increases reproductive opportunities, suggesting instead that cognitive and behavioral integration may override narrow fitness signals.
points: Men with higher fluid intelligence showed both greater physical markers of fitness (grip strength, shoulder-hip ratio) and yet reported fewer casual sexual partners, contradicting assumptions about fitness and mating.

The study measured cognitive ability through computerized pattern recognition tasks and assessed sexual behavior through standardized questionnaires tracking actual sexual history rather than attitudes.
The findings suggest that integrated cognitive-behavioral development may lead men away from transactional sexual relationships despite physical attractiveness markers.
quotes: Young men with higher fluid intelligence also tend to display markers of general physical fitness, such as grip strength and a more V-shaped torso, while reporting fewer casual sexual partners.
Fluid intelligence refers to the ability to reason, recognize patterns, and solve new problems independently of prior learned knowledge.

A higher shoulder-to-hip ratio typically indicates a more V-shaped, muscular torso, which evolutionary biologists often view as a marker of physical health.” Archived from PsyPost on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
